title: Can the China-US Detente Last?
author: Yao Bowen
text:
U.S. President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping of China arrive via the Cross Hall to a State Arrival ceremony on the State Floor of the White House, Sep. 24, 2026.
Credit: Official White House Photo by Daniel Torok
The recent thaw in China-U.S. relations – highlighted by reciprocal visits by President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping – raised the prospect of a more stable relationship between the world’s two largest powers. After years of escalating tariffs, technology restrictions, and strategic mistrust, both governments appear willing to step back from the brink. The emerging language of “constructive strategic stability” suggests that Washington and Beijing may be converging on the need to manage their rivalry rather than allow it to define every aspect of their relationship.But agreement on the need to manage competition is not the same as agreement on its terms. The two sides may have reached a shared conclusion that escalation is too costly without resolving the underlying disputes that drove them toward confrontation in the first place. If so, the current detente could prove less a turning point than a temporary adjustment in a much longer strategic contest.[...]
